title: Game of Gates
author: Bobqcarter
selftext:
I asked an AI like a year ago how long until I can just type what I want a game to be and get a game, and it said five years. Tonight, I typed, in very great detail, exactly this board game I designed a long time ago, and it crapped out the HTML nearly instantly. It did one thing wrong then, after prompting, it fixed it. I loaded the game to my site and it worked! I'm blown away. I asked it if it could make it rudimentary multiplayer, where if two people are on the site, the first one to click white sets the sides. And that worked too! I'm blown away. [GameofGates.com](http://GameofGates.com) \-It's janky, but I was about to pay a guy on fiverr a thousand bucks to make just this a year ago and Gemini did it in seconds.  
Rules: Turn a gate, move your piece, get to the other side square in the corner or pin your opponent against the edge so they can't move.

It's still a little janky, because there are no rails, but hey, its my game on the web!

comments.author: hushzephyr
comments.body:
Congrats on finding the tool to bring your idea to life!

Gameplay feels a bit repetitive at the moment though — it's mostly just opening a gap to get to the next row. It could be a lot more fun with more variety, but that would be quite a bit of extra work.

Also, once the complexity scales up, relying solely on AI might hit some limits — you might find it's not as smart as you'd expect...

replies.author: Bobqcarter
replies.body:
AI so far doesn't get it at all. The opening is for sure the most tedious part but there are a few techniques that we've come up with that make it important, like closing gates behind the piece to open up new rows. It gets a lot more interesting and challenging once the pieces get to the middle. Then its mostly make paths while using one's piece as a blocker, then a sneaky turn can open up a huge line around the back. I've had companies play it and not get it, but I've played it a lot of times with my nephew and we've never drawn. Here's a game where black was about to pin white back into their corner, but white had the turn to open up a path all the way to black's square.
